details: Bitcoin continued its slide, dipping below $80,000 on Friday afternoon, following hotter-than-expected US inflation reports earlier in the week. US tech stocks also fell sharply, contributing to a broader risk-off environment. Altcoins experienced "outsized drawdowns" compared to Bitcoin, with the total crypto market cap declining. Futures traders added new bets despite falling prices, and those betting on a rise paid more to keep positions open. The Federal Reserve's late-October decision is seen as the next major test for market direction.
title: US Inflation Pressures Bitcoin and Altcoins, Driving Risk-Off Sentiment

details: Bloomberg Intelligence strategist Mike McGlone predicted Bitcoin could fall to $10,000 if US stocks, specifically the S&P 500, drop 20%, citing market and bond yield pressures. Countering this, Cryptoquant CEO Ki Young Ju argued that a $30,000 floor is more realistic, supported by $58 billion in ETF inflows and 1.3 million BTC held by treasuries. The Nasdaq 100's performance will be a key indicator for McGlone's scenario.
title: Bitcoin Price Floor Debate: Bloomberg vs. Cryptoquant CEO

details: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde, in her statement to the IMF's monetary committee, urged lawmakers to adopt digital euro regulation by late 2026. She also highlighted the Eurosystem's new tokenized-settlement platform, Pontes, which went live on September 21, linking tokenized asset trades to Eurosystem settlement using central bank money. Lagarde noted that rising energy prices are expected to keep Eurozone inflation above the ECB's target until mid-2027, with September inflation reaching 3.8%.
title: ECB Pushes Digital Euro and Tokenized Settlement Amid Inflation Concerns

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) reported that tokenized real-world assets (RWA), excluding stablecoins and repos, reached approximately $65 billion by July. While acknowledging the benefits of faster transactions, the IMF warned of increasing liquidity risks and leverage stemming from tokenized assets. It noted that programmable collateral, automated margin calls, and continuous trading could accelerate forced liquidations during market distress, and identified legal certainty, regulatory clarity, interoperability, and reliable settlement assets as obstacles to adoption.
title: IMF Warns of Risks in Growing Tokenized Real-World Asset Market

details: Deutsche Bank is set to launch its first digital asset service, focusing on crypto custody. The initial rollout in Germany will support major cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum, with plans to expand into Asian financial centers next year. This move is part of the bank's strategy to grow its corporate banking sector and tap into the digital economy, including stablecoins and blockchain-based securities.
title: Deutsche Bank to Launch Crypto Custody, Targets Asian Expansion

details: A Wall Street Journal investigation alleged that Tether paid approximately $6.3 million to a consulting firm partly owned by Bo Hines, who was a senior White House cryptocurrency official. Hines reportedly helped advance the GENIUS Act, legislation with significant implications for Tether, before leaving government to become the stablecoin issuer's US chief executive. His firm, Nxum, denies any improper involvement.
title: Tether Under Scrutiny Over Payments to Former White House Official's Firm

details: Major US companies, including Verizon, UnitedHealth Group, and Broadcom, have reportedly objected to the tokenization of their own shares under a new regulatory framework. This opposition highlights potential conflicts of interest and challenges in the expansion of tokenized securities. The crypto market is expected to trade sideways if risk appetite recovers, but further weakness, especially in altcoins, is anticipated if opposition to regulation spreads.
title: US Companies Oppose Tokenization of Their Own Shares

details: Payward, the parent company of cryptocurrency exchange Kraken, is acquiring Lithuania's Saldo Bank. This acquisition marks Payward as the first digital asset firm to purchase a bank in Europe. The aim is to unify cash, crypto, tokenized stocks, and credit into a single system, allowing clients to borrow against assets without selling them. Saldo Bank holds an EU banking license and offers consumer loans, business loans, and term deposits.
title: Payward (Kraken) Acquires Saldo Bank to Integrate Crypto and Traditional Finance
